candidates.tagline: Lake Ontario has been renamed 'Lake America.' The lake has not complied.
candidates.story: On August 29, 2026, Trump signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario 'Lake America' as part of escalating trade tensions with Canada; Google Maps immediately updated it for U.S. users, while Canadian maps still say 'Lake Ontario' — making the same body of water officially three different names at once.
candidates.why_funny: Renaming a 400-year-old Great Lake by executive order doesn't change the water, the fish, or what Canadians see on their side of the border — it just means the most-used map app now disagrees with itself at the shoreline.
candidates.alt: Family walking past a bilingual roadside sign reading 'Lake Ontario, Now and Always' in English and French near Grimsby, Ontario, on August 29 2026, in response to the Trump administration's executive order renaming the lake

candidates.tagline: Apple redesigned Safari's compass icon. It now has two needles. Compasses have one.
candidates.story: iOS 27 Beta 5 shipped in August 2026 with a redesigned Safari compass icon featuring a centre pin that makes the red and white needle tips appear to be two separate, independently-spinning pointers — like clock hands — rather than the single bipolar needle of a real compass; the design went viral on August 24–25 with critics noting the icon seems to have been designed by someone who has never seen a compass.
candidates.why_funny: Apple spent months crafting 'Liquid Glass' icons to more faithfully represent real-world objects, then shipped a compass whose physics suggest the north needle and south needle can point wherever they like.
candidates.alt: Apple's iOS 27 Safari browser icon in the Liquid Glass redesign, showing a compass whose overlapping red and white needle tips look like two separate independently-spinning pointers rather than a single bipolar needle
